page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8581C cores operating at 2.3 GHz, with hyperthreading enabled. The system is equipped with 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.75 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions and Advanced Vector Extensions.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core execution. The instance demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2258.0 and a strong single-threaded gzip compression rate of 35.11 GB/sec. However, multi-core and parallel execution metrics are comparatively limited, with stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores falling into the weak category. Memory performance also shows a clear division: cached read-only memory bandwidth is average at 344.16 GB/sec, whereas uncached large-block read and write speeds are weak, measuring 32.39 GB/sec and 20.69 GB/sec respectively.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative resource density for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is suited for single-threaded text processing, basic web serving, and lightweight LLM inference, where it achieves average prompt processing speeds of 33.72 tokens/sec on 7B models. Conversely, it is less efficient for heavy multi-threaded compiling, database operations, or high-throughput Redis deployments due to its lower multi-core and uncached memory write benchmarks.
